'''''Rumex maderensis''''', commonly known as '''Madeira sorrel'''<ref name="inaturalist-Rumex maderensis" /> or '''Madeira dock''',<ref name="FloraTeide2025" /> is a [[species]] of flowering plant in the buckwheat family [[Polygonaceae]].<ref name="inaturalist-Rumex maderensis">{{cite web |title=Madeira sorrel (Rumex maderensis) |url=https://www.inaturalist.org/taxa/699253-Rumex-maderensis |website=iNaturalist |access-date=6 December 2025 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Description==
''Rumex maderensis'' is a [[subshrub]] with [[Ovate (botany)|ovate]]-[[Deltoid leaf|deltoid]] leaves, that wither at the base. It has simple [[inflorescence]]s with unisexual flowers, that consist of six perianth segments arranged in two rows. Its fruits are small nuts with membranous, suborbicular valves enclosing it. Both the flowering and fruiting period lasts from sprint to summer with both being wind dispersed. The chromosomal count of the plant is 2n = 40.<ref name="FloraTeide2025" />

==Range==
The plant grows on [[Madeira Island]] and the Western [[Canary Islands]] of [[Tenerife]], [[Gran Canaria]], [[La Palma]], [[La Gomera]] and [[El Hierro]].
In the [[Teide National Park]] it grows on the Western slopes of the [[Montaña de Igueque]], in altitudes of about 2100 m.<ref name="FloraTeide2025" />

==Habitat==
It can mostly be found in the Thermo- and Meso-Mediterranean bioclimatic zones on rocky, humid and shady slopes and [[ravine]]s, open formation or stony terrain.<ref name="FloraTeide2025" />

==Ecology==
''Rumex maderensis'' is characteristic of the botanical assemblage known as the [[Ranunculo cortusifolii-Geranion canariensis alliance]].<ref name="FloraTeide2025" />

==Uses==
In folk medicine ''R. maderensis'' is used in [[poultice]]s for [[dermatosis]] and in [[infusion]]s as a [[diuretic]] and blood depurative.<ref name="Tavares2010">{{cite journal | last1 = Tavares| first1 = Lucélia| last2 = Carrilho| first2 = Dina| last3 = Tyagi| first3 = Meenu| last4 = Barata| first4 = David| last5 = Serra| first5 = Ana Teresa| last6 = Duarte| first6 = Catarina Maria Martins| last7 = Duarte| first7 = Rui Oliveira| last8 = Feliciano| first8 = Rodrigo Pedro| last9 = Bronze| first9 = Maria Rosário| last10 = Chicau| first10 = Paula| title = Antioxidant capacity of macaronesian traditional medicinal plants | journal = Molecules | date = 2010-04-12| volume = 15| issue = 4| pages = 2576–2592 | issn = 1420-3049 | doi = 10.3390/molecules15042576  | pmid = 20428065 |doi-access=free| pmc = 6257369}}</ref>

==Biochemistry==
86 [[polyphenol]]s and 9 non-phenolic compounds were identied in menthanol extracts of leaves, flowers and stems using [[HPLC–MS]], with flowers and leaves having the highest polyphenol content. [[Vitexin]] isomers, [[apigenin-8-C-hexoside-O-rhamnoside]] and [[isoorientin]] were the most common polyphenols in leaves an flowers, with stems having high contents of [[proanthocyanidin]]s. Even after in vitro digestion extracts showed activity against [[free radical]]s with leaf and flower extract exerting the highest activity.<ref name="Spínola2018">{{cite journal | last1 = Spínola| first1 = Vítor| last2 = Llorent-Martínez| first2 = Eulogio J.| last3 = Castilho| first3 = Paula C.| title = Antioxidant polyphenols of Madeira sorrel (Rumex maderensis): How do they survive to in vitro simulated gastrointestinal digestion? | journal = Food Chemistry | date = 2018-09-01| volume = 259| pages = 105–112 | issn = 1873-7072 | doi = 10.1016/j.foodchem.2018.03.112  | pmid = 29680032| url = https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0308814618305545| url-access = subscription| hdl = 10400.13/3204| hdl-access = free}}</ref>
The presence of [[Vitamin C]] in the plant was confirmed by enzymatic method.<ref name="Tavares2010" />
